newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates edge up further, guilder weak.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates edge up further, guilder weak.

text.p: Dutch money market rates continued their way up on Tuesday in anticipation of a possible rate hike as recent guilder weakness against the mark persisted.
Call money changed hands between 3.18 and 3.25 percent, some six basis points higher than on Monday, dealers said.
Other guilder deposit rates were all up two basis points, with three month-deposits set at 3.26/34 bid/ask and one year-deposits at 3.46/54 percent.
Market players were closely watching the guilder, which hovered around its Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) central rate of 112.673 marks per 100 guilders, sometimes crossing it.
But dealers were divided over the chances of a unilateral rate hike by the Dutch central bank on Thursday to support the guilder.

"The central bank is definitely taking a good look at it," one dealer said, adding market players expected the special advances rate to be raised 10 basis points to 3.10 percent if the guilder solidly crossed the central rate.
"The guilder is really getting into the danger zone, and it's not impossible the central bank might consider a move," another said.
The weakening of the guilder has increased the likelihood of a Dutch rate hike in the near future, but the Dutch might wait for Germany's Bundesbank to take the lead, a third trader said.
"It's obvious something will have to be done if the uptrend continues," he added.
He said a move in the special advances rate would probably trigger a hike in the secured loans or fixed advance rate, currently set at 2.50 percent.
"Otherwise, the gap between the two gets too big," he said.
Sales under the new Dutch Treasury Certificate (DTC) programme maturing on October 31, which started today, were progressing satisfactorily, a finance ministry official said.
"There's good demand for all DTCs, but a little more for the new programme," he said, adding October DTCs had been placed at the screen price of 3.24 percent.
Indicative prices for DTCs maturing in August and September were set at 3.22 percent, for the December paper at 3.26 percent and for paper running until June next year at 3.35 percent.
"These prices are nicely in line with the market," one dealer said.
